tools.description:
Resolve a transported-hazmat incident against the ERG 2024.

Returns the ID number, names, ERG guide number and title, whether ERG Table 1
lists the material (TIH), its hazard class rule set, its 49 CFR 172.101 hazard
class and label codes, its CAMEO datasheets, which ERG table gives its distances
(Table 1, Table 3, or the guide's EVACUATION distances), and whether the
incident time is day or night at the point, with the sunrise and sunset. Each
value has a `basis` entry: a source tag and the page it reads.

Data source: ERG 2024, 49 CFR 172.101 and CAMEO, from the server's packs.
Update cadence: changes only with a server release. As-of: `pack_versions`.
Every ERG ID number resolves; full rows (distances, CFR, CAMEO, hazard class)
exist for the seed materials, and any other ID returns `coverage: erg`.

A load with no ID number or name (`placard` or `guide_number` instead of
`material`) returns `coverage: unidentified`: the guide the ERG's Table of
Markings, Labels and Placards circles beside the placard (or the guide given),
`identified_by` saying how, no material, and `tih` null. An explosive the
yellow index names with no ID number ("Blasting agent", "ANFO") returns
`coverage: unnumbered` the same way, with the index page. An input the ERG
cannot answer returns `error` and a `hint`, never a guess.
tools.name: assess_incident

incident.description:
A transported-hazmat incident as reported. The load is given by exactly one of
`material`, `placard` and `guide_number`: the ERG's Table of Markings, Labels and
Placards is for "when the ID number or proper shipping name is not available" (ERG
2024 PDF p. 9).

container.description: An ERG Table 3 container kind (Rail tank car; Highway tank truck or trailer; Agricultural nurse tank; Multiple ton cylinders; Multiple small cylinders; Multiple small cylinders or single ton cylinder), a unique start of one (highway tank truck), or unknown.

guide_number.description: For a load with no ID number or name: an ERG orange guide number, such as 111 (Mixed Load/Unidentified Cargo), 112 (explosives, Divisions 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5) or 114 (Divisions 1.4, 1.6).

incident_time.description: When, ISO 8601 with a UTC offset (2026-10-21T14:05:00-04:00). Decides day or night for the ERG tables.

material.description: The ID number from the placard or shipping paper (UN1017, NA1993 or 1017), or the material name as the ERG yellow index prints it (Chlorine; a generic name may drop its ', n.o.s.'; an explosive the index lists by name, such as 'Blasting agent' or ANFO, resolves to its guide). Omit it when the material is not identified, and give `placard` or `guide_number`.

placard.description: For a load with no ID number or name: the placard as read, which the ERG's Table of Markings, Labels and Placards sends to a guide. The class or division printed on it (2.3, 1.4, 8), a word printed on it (FLAMMABLE GAS, OXYGEN, GASOLINE), DANGEROUS, or none when hazardous materials are suspected and no placard can be seen. A class whose divisions have their own guides (2, 4, 5, 6) returns the candidates.

spill_size.description: small: 208 liters (55 US gallons) or less; large: more than 208 liters (55 US gallons); unknown: the large spill distances apply.

where_spilled.description: The surface the spill is on. It changes the answer only for a material ERG Table 2 lists (water-reactive): in water its Table 1 entry printed "(when spilled in water)" applies; on land a material Table 1 lists only for water is answered by its guide. land is the default, as in PHMSA's ERG app (whereSpilled).

tools.description:
The ERG zones for an incident, as GeoJSON with their distances and sources.

For a material ERG Table 1 lists: the initial isolation zone (a circle) and the
protective action zone, the ERG's own square (its side is the protective action
distance, downwind, the spill at the midpoint of its upwind side), from the
Table 1 or Table 3 row for the spill size, day or night and wind band. That
square is the only downwind shape the ERG gives. For any other material: the
guide's immediate precautionary distance as a circle. A guide's downwind
evacuation distance for a large spill (`zones.large_spill_downwind`) has no
shape in the ERG, so none is drawn; do not draw one. With fire, the guide's
isolation distance for a tank in fire, as a circle. Returns the distances in
metres and as the ERG prints them, the table row used, the wind used (value,
band, as-of, source), day or night, and `basis` source tags.
`incident.where_spilled` (land, the default, or water) selects a water-reactive
material's Table 1 entry for a spill in water (ERG Table 2). `flags` are the
fired flag rules, each with its sentence and receipts. A load known only by its
placard or a guide number (`placard` or `guide_number` instead of `material`)
gets that guide's circles and no Table 1 zone, which `limits` says.

A load the ERG answers with several candidates (a name under several ID
numbers, an ID number whose names carry different guides, a placard that
matches several rows) is drawn once per candidate: `ambiguity.candidates` holds
each candidate's zones, guide and locators, and the one with the largest
distances is `governing` (the ERG's rule: the most conservative guide). The top
level is the governing candidate's answer, except that `footprint` holds every
candidate's polygons (each with its `candidate` and `governing`), `flags` adds
`ambiguous_material`, and `limits` holds every candidate's. Nothing is
averaged. Name every candidate, and identify the material to settle it.

`verify_in_erg_app` is PHMSA's ERG app link for the same scenario; `limits` says
what it and the inputs cannot do (the app may draw ERG 2020 distances).

Data source: ERG 2024 (the server's packs); wind from `wind` if given, else the
National Weather Service forecast grid for the point (api.weather.gov), the
period holding the incident time. Update cadence: NWS revises the grid through
the day. As-of: `wind.as_of` and the NWS response headers. No dispersion model;
nothing is interpolated. An input the ERG cannot answer returns `error` and a
`hint`.
tools.name: protective_action_footprint

tools.description:
Who is inside a footprint: residents (night), jobs (day), group quarters by
type, people 65 and over, people with a disability, households with no
vehicle, limited English speaking households, and the Community Resilience
Estimates count, each with its margin of error where the source has one.

Pass `area.footprint`, the GeoJSON protective_action_footprint returns (or any
polygon), the incident time, and optionally its `day_night.period`. Blocks
partly inside count by the share of their area inside. Both day and night
counts are always returned; `primary` says which the period makes first.

Data sources: TIGERweb 2020 tabulation blocks, block groups and tracts; the
2020 Census DHC (P1, P18) by block; the ACS 2020-2024 5-year by block group
or tract; LEHD LODES8 workplace area characteristics 2023 (cached state
files); Community Resilience Estimates 2024 by tract (api.census.gov).
Update cadence: ACS and CRE annual, LODES annual, the 2020 counts fixed.
As-of: each count's `as_of` and the `basis` source tags. Requires
CENSUS_API_KEY; without it, returns `error` with the signup URL.
tools.name: population_at_risk

area.description: The area to count people in, and when.

footprint.description: GeoJSON: the `footprint` FeatureCollection protective_action_footprint returns, a Feature, or a Polygon or MultiPolygon in WGS84 longitude and latitude. Points and lines are ignored; the polygons are counted as one area.

incident_time.description: When, ISO 8601 with a UTC offset. Decides day or night when `period` is not given.

period.description: The ERG period, as protective_action_footprint's `day_night.period` gives it. Omitted: computed from `incident_time` at the footprint.

zones.description: Count only these footprint zones (`properties.zone`, such as protective_action_zone). Omitted: every polygon in the footprint.

tools.description:
The schools, hospitals, nursing homes, emergency services (fire, EMS,
ambulance, police), waterways and rail lines and grade crossings inside a
footprint, each with its zone (isolation or protective_action; else the guide
circle it is in: large_spill_evacuation, fire_isolation or fire_evacuation),
source id and as-of.

Pass `area.footprint`, the GeoJSON protective_action_footprint returns (or any
polygon), and optionally `buffer_m`. Group quarters residents are counted by
population_at_risk, not here. `flag_inputs` carries the counts the facility
flag rules read; this tool fires no flag.

Data sources: USGS National Structures Dataset (carto.nationalmap.gov; schools,
colleges, hospitals, fire and EMS stations, ambulance services, police
stations); CMS Nursing Home Provider Information (cached file); USGS 3D
Hydrography Program flowlines and waterbodies (hydro.nationalmap.gov); BTS NTAD
North American Rail Network Lines and FRA Railroad Grade Crossings
(services.arcgis.com). Update cadence: Structures and 3DHP refreshed by USGS
(3DHP quarterly), NTAD as FRA updates, CMS quarterly. As-of: each facility's
`as_of` (its load date) and the `basis` source tags. A source that fails is
listed in `errors` and the others still answer.
tools.name: facilities_in_footprint

area.description: The area to list facilities, waterways and rail in.

buffer_m.description: Grow the footprint by this many metres before listing. 0 by default: the ERG zones are the zones.

footprint.description: GeoJSON: the `footprint` FeatureCollection protective_action_footprint returns (its zones are read from `properties.zone`), a Feature, or a Polygon or MultiPolygon in WGS84 longitude and latitude.

tools.description:
Hospitals with emergency services outside the footprint, nearest first by
straight-line distance from the footprint's upwind edge, with beds, type,
distance, bearing, and `crosses_footprint` when the straight line from that
edge runs through the footprint (a hospital reached only through the zone).
Hospitals inside the footprint are listed apart, as casualty sites.

Pass `incident.location` (the spill point), `incident.footprint` (the GeoJSON
protective_action_footprint returns) and optionally `max_km` (50 km by
default). Distances are straight-line, not drive time; trauma level and burn
or toxicology capability are not in these datasets.

Data sources: CMS Hospital General Information (emergency services, type)
joined to CMS Provider of Services (beds) on the CCN, placed by the Census
Geocoder and, where it fails, by the USGS National Structures Dataset hospital
at the same address (a file cached by scripts/fetch_cms.py; no call per
incident). Update cadence: CMS quarterly. As-of: the `basis` source tags.
tools.name: receiving_hospitals

incident.description: The spill and its footprint, to find hospitals outside it.

footprint.description: GeoJSON: the `footprint` FeatureCollection protective_action_footprint returns (its zones are read from `properties.zone`), a Feature, or a Polygon or MultiPolygon in WGS84 longitude and latitude.

max_km.description: Search radius in kilometres from the footprint's upwind edge. Omitted: 50 km.

tools.description:
What to do about this material: its ERG orange guide by section (potential
hazards; public safety; emergency response), each a list of lines `{text, page,
kind, locator, quotation}` as the ERG prints them, in printed order,
sub-headings kept.

The incident selects the lines: with `fire_involved` the fire subsection comes
first and the guide's fire evacuation is printed; `spill_size` keeps the Small
Spill or the Large Spill lines (unknown keeps both); `where_spilled` water adds
the Table 2 note for a water-reactive material; the sentence on materials
"designated with a (P)" only when the guide number carries the P.
`selection.omitted` names every line left out and why. `general_first_aid` names
the ERG section the guide refers to, with its page.

For a load known only by its placard or a guide number (`placard` or
`guide_number` instead of `material`), the guide the ERG's Table of Markings,
Labels and Placards gives, with `identified_by` saying how and `material` null.

Data source: ERG 2024 orange guides (the server's packs). Update cadence: with a
server release. As-of: `pack_versions`. No network call, no model. An unknown
material returns `error` with a `hint` and the nearest index names.
tools.name: material_response_guidance

tools.description:
A draft ICS 201 Incident Briefing (FEMA ICS Form 201) for the incident: the
blocks public data can fill, block by block, every sentence with its receipts,
plus a Markdown rendering and a GeoJSON map for Block 4. The blocks that are the
Incident Commander's (2 Incident Number, 8 Current and Planned Actions,
Strategies, and Tactics, 9 Current Organization, and the names and signature of
Block 6) are blank and labelled.

Pass `request.incident` (as for protective_action_footprint), optionally `wind`
and `incident_name`. The server runs assess_incident,
protective_action_footprint, population_at_risk, facilities_in_footprint,
receiving_hospitals and material_response_guidance on it and fires the flag
rules over their outputs; Block 5 prints at most ten fired flags, high priority
first, each as the value it fired on, then its ERG consequence and its ERG
response. A load the ERG answers with several candidates is briefed as
protective_action_footprint draws it: Block 1 and Block 5 name every candidate,
the distances are the governing (largest) candidate's, and the sketch dashes
the others. Block 10 tables the nearest five receiving hospitals. Annex A,
after the form, lists every limit and every source with its as-of. A tool that
fails is listed in `errors`, its lines say so, and the other blocks still fill.
`response_format` concise (the default) returns the Markdown form, every
sentence with its source tag, the GeoJSON, `errors` and `pack_versions`;
detailed adds `blocks` (each sentence with its receipts), `annex` and `flags`,
60,000 to 100,000 characters in all, above Claude Code's default cap on a tool
result. With detailed, `request.block` returns one part (a block by number,
annex or flags), at most about 28,000 characters; ask for each part in turn.
`include_tool_outputs` returns the outputs the receipts point into.

Block 4's sketch, with `include_map_svg`, is `map_svg`, an SVG the Markdown
embeds as `ics201_block4.svg`: save it beside the Markdown under that name to
view the two together. With it the result is over 100,000 characters, above
Claude Code's default cap on a tool result. `geojson` carries the same
features for a client that draws.

Data sources: those tools' (ERG 2024 packs; NWS wind; Census DHC, ACS, LODES,
CRE; USGS Structures and 3DHP; CMS; NTAD rail), and TIGERweb (the place and
county at the spill, January 1, 2026 vintage; the roads image, as of the day it
is retrieved). Update cadence and as-of: each sentence's source tag and Annex
A. No model writes any sentence; nothing is interpolated.
tools.name: build_ics_201

request.description: The incident to draft an ICS 201 for.

block.description: With response_format detailed, return only this part with its receipts: a block by its number (1 to 10), annex (Annex A) or flags (every fired flag). A part is at most about 28,000 characters. Omitted: the whole detailed form, 60,000 to 100,000 characters, above Claude Code's default cap on a tool result (25,000 tokens).
